Here is the structured extraction of James W. Aageson's distinct positions and claims across the twelve B001 items from his doctoral thesis (Paul's Use of Scripture, Oxford University, 1983).
B001-1: Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
S01F-E001
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E001
B001 Passage ID: B001-1
Author's Claim: Paul transposes the word order of ἐπίστευσεν and Ἀβραάμ between Romans 4:3 and Galatians 3:6, exhibiting minor inconsistency in quotation form without altering the fundamental textual meaning
1
.
Supporting Quotation: "the words euLaieuoev and 'A$paoty have been transposed. The variations in the last two examples do not affect the sense of the texts"
1
.
Printed Page Number: Page 70 (p. 85, fn. 69)
1
NotebookLM Citation:
1
Textual Evidence Invoked: Word order of Genesis 15:6 LXX in Romans 4:3 (Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ) versus Galatians 3:6 (Ἀβραὰμ ἐπίστευσεν)
1
.
Claim Type: Textual-critical
Qualifications / Conditions: The author explicitly notes that this word-order transposition does not alter the underlying semantic sense
1
.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
S01F-E002
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E002
B001 Passage ID: B001-1
Author's Claim: Paul utilizes the narrative sequence of Genesis 15:6 in Romans 4:3 to demonstrate that Abraham was reckoned righteous prior to his circumcision, deriving a theological principle from the literary order [202, 240–241].
Supporting Quotation: "In this text, Paul's emphasis on the literary sequence of the Genesis narrative has enabled him to use scripture to support his distinction between righteousness by faith and circumcision."
2
Printed Page Number: Page 138–139 (p. 202)
2
NotebookLM Citation:
2
Textual Evidence Invoked: Chronological sequence of Genesis 15:6 (faith reckoned as righteousness) relative to Genesis 17 (institution of circumcision) in Romans 4:3–12 [202, 240–241].
Claim Type: Exegetical
Qualifications / Conditions: The author notes that while Paul's selective emphasis yields an altered understanding of the narrative, Paul believed he was uncovering the true sense
2
3
.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-2: Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23
S01F-E003
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E003
B001 Passage ID: B001-2
Author's Claim: Paul follows the textual tradition represented by Codex Vaticanus (LXX-B) in employing forms of ἀγαπάω (ἠγαπημένην) rather than Codex Alexandrinus (LXX-A), which reads forms of ἐλεέω (ἠλεημένην)
4
.
Supporting Quotation: "Paul and LXX-B have forms of ayomav, whereas LXX-A uses forms of eXeetv"
4
.
Printed Page Number: Page 69 (fn. 19)
4
NotebookLM Citation:
4
Textual Evidence Invoked: Variant readings in Hosea 2:23 (25) between LXX-B (ἠγαπημένην) and LXX-A (ἠλεημένην) compared with Romans 9:25
4
.
Claim Type: Textual-critical
Qualifications / Conditions: None
4
.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
S01F-E004
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E004
B001 Passage ID: B001-2
Author's Claim: Paul deliberately substitutes καλέσω for ἐρῶ in Hosea 2:23 (LXX 2:25) to forge a verbal catchword connection with κληθήσονται in Hosea 1:10 (LXX 2:1) and the overarching theme of divine calling in Romans 9:6–24 [81, 299–300].
Supporting Quotation: "The substitution of xaXeaw for epw in the citation from Hosea 2:25 LXX, has resulted in a verbal connection in Paul's text between the two Hosea passages"
5
.
Printed Page Number: Page 81 (p. 178 / p. 299)
5
6

5

Claim Type: Literary
Qualifications / Conditions: Presented as the probable motivation explaining the text modification

B001-3: Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10
S01F-E005
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E005
B001 Passage ID: B001-3
Author's Claim: Paul's wording in Romans 9:26 exhibits direct textual agreement with Codex Alexandrinus (LXX-A) in its reading of Hosea 1:10 (LXX 2:1)

.

Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E006
B001 Passage ID: B001-3
Author's Claim: The phrase υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος in Hosea 1:10 (quoted in Rom 9:26) functions as a catchword verbal link with υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ in the juxtaposed citation of Isaiah 10:22–23 in Romans 9:27 [303–304].
Supporting Quotation: "The verbal link is between uioi SeotJ CUJVTOS in 9:26 and UL(5v 'lopci^X in 9:27."

Claim Type: Literary

S01F-E007
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E007
B001 Passage ID: B001-4
Author's Claim: Paul's inclusion of ἐπʼ αὐτῷ in Romans 10:11 (and Rom 9:33) aligns with the Greek textual tradition preserved in Codex Alexandrinus (LXX-A), against Codex Vaticanus (LXX-B)

B001 Passage ID: B001-4

S01F-E009
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E009
B001 Passage ID: B001-5
Author's Claim: Paul cites Joel 2:32 (LXX 3:5) in Romans 10:13 not as an adoption of an early Church Pentecost tradition (as in Acts 2:21), but as a scriptural proof built on the key terms πᾶς and ἐπικαλέω to demonstrate universal salvation [193–194].
Supporting Quotation: "The two words, nSs and enuxaXeuadau are key words for Paul, and they assist him in developing an argument concerning the salvation of both Jews and Greeks."

S01F-E010
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E010
B001 Passage ID: B001-6
Author's Claim: Paul's word order σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ in Romans 11:34 (and 1 Cor 2:16) follows Codex Alexandrinus (LXX-A), whereas Codex Vaticanus (LXX-B) transposes the terms (αὐτοῦ σύμβουλος)

B001 Passage ID: B001-6

S01F-E012
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E012
B001 Passage ID: B001-7
Author's Claim: Paul quotes Isaiah 11:10 in Romans 15:12 within a scriptural catena structured around the catchword ἔθνη to substantiate Christ's role in the hope and election of the Gentiles

B001-8: 1 Corinthians 1:19 / Isaiah 29:14
S01F-E013
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E013
B001 Passage ID: B001-8
Author's Claim: Paul cites Isaiah 29:14 in 1 Corinthians 1:19 as a thematic and verbal catalyst that generates his entire exposition on God making foolish the wisdom of the world [102–103].
Supporting Quotation: "the scriptural citation is related not only to the opening statement but also contributes thematically and verbally to the discussion that follows." [102–103].
Printed Page Number: Page 91–92 (p. 102–103)

NotebookLM Citation:

Textual Evidence Invoked: Citation of Isa 29:14 in 1 Cor 1:19 followed by thematic elaboration in 1 Cor 1:20–25 using σοφία and σοφῶν [102–103].
Claim Type: Literary
Qualifications / Conditions: The author acknowledges E. Earle Ellis's thesis that 1 Cor 1:18–31 may derive from an earlier Jewish midrashic unit adopted by Paul

Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-9: 1 Corinthians 6:16 / Genesis 2:24
S01F-E014
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E014
B001 Passage ID: B001-9
Author's Claim: The sole textual divergence between Paul's double citation of Genesis 2:24 in 1 Corinthians 6:16 and Ephesians 5:31 is the parenthetical insertion of the formula γάρ, φησίν in 1 Corinthians for syntactical integration
21
.
Supporting Quotation: "the only difference between the two references is that the introductory formula, yap (prioov, has been included for syntactical reasons"

Printed Page Number: Page 70–71 (p. 83–84)

Textual Evidence Invoked: Text of Gen 2:24 in 1 Cor 6:16 (Ἔσονται γάρ, φησίν, οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν) compared with Eph 5:31
21
.
Claim Type: Textual-critical
Qualifications / Conditions: Minor stylistic omission of αὐτοῦ in Eph 5:31 does not affect the core structural agreement [59–60, 84].
Extraction Confidence: HIGH

Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E015
B001 Passage ID: B001-9
Author's Claim: Paul applies Genesis 2:24 in 1 Corinthians 6:16 as an ethical halakic command regulating sexual conduct, illustrating the application of narrative creation tradition to behavioral instruction
22
.
Supporting Quotation: "In four instances, "narrative" passages are used in contexts which pertain to ethics; 120I Cor. 6:16 (Gen. 2:24)..."

Printed Page Number: Page 104 (p. 156)

Qualifications / Conditions: None

S01F-E016
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E016
B001 Passage ID: B001-10
Author's Claim: Paul cites Deuteronomy 25:4 in 1 Corinthians 9:9 with the lexical variant κημώσεις (for φιμώσεις) and applies it via an explicit exegetical question (διʼ ἡμᾶς) to validate an apostle's right to material support

Printed Page Number: Page 93 (p. 107, p. 149 / p. 244)

B001-11: 1 Corinthians 10:7 / Exodus 32:6
S01F-E017
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E017
B001 Passage ID: B001-11
Author's Claim: Paul cites Exodus 32:6 in 1 Corinthians 10:7 within a midrashic parenetic framework, utilizing Israel's wilderness experience as a moral warning (τύπος) against idolatry rather than as formal historical typology [249–250, 257].
Supporting Quotation: "the use of TUUOS and TUTILMWS in the sense of 'warning' or 'example' in I Corinthians 10:6-13 provides little support for the view that Paul's use of scripture is fundamentally typological."
26
.
Printed Page Number: Page 150 (p. 249–250, p. 257)
26
27
NotebookLM Citation:
26
27
Textual Evidence Invoked: Citation of Exod 32:6 ("the people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play") in 1 Cor 10:7 framed by τυπικῶς and νουθεσία in 1 Cor 10:6, 11
26
27
.
Claim Type: Exegetical
Qualifications / Conditions: The author acknowledges possible sacramental typology in 1 Cor 10:1–4, but maintains that 10:6–13 is primarily ethical and parenetic
26
.
Extraction Confidence: HIGH
B001-12: Galatians 3:13 / Deuteronomy 21:23
S01F-E018
Proposed Evidence ID: S01F-E018
B001 Passage ID: B001-12
Author's Claim: In Galatians 3:13, Paul (or a pre-Pauline tradition) deliberately omits ὑπὸ θεοῦ from Deuteronomy 21:23 LXX to avoid implying that Christ was accursed by God [74–75, 288].
Supporting Quotation: "his text omits the words UTIO deoti... likely that they were omitted in order to avoid presenting an unacceptable image of the divine."

.
Printed Page Number: Page 80 (p. 74–75, p. 288)
28

Title: Paul's Use of Scripture: A Comparative Study of Biblical Interpretation in Early Palestinian Judaism and the New Testament With Special Reference to Romans 9-11
James W. Aageson
Mansfield College, the University of Oxford
Doctor of Philosophy

Second, it is argued that Paul's method of scriptural interpretation and argumentation is fundamental to the theological development of the discussion in Romans 9-11.
